task_description: Help me draft an email from our CEO to department heads about a company-wide hiring freeze — the CEO is direct but empathetic, and the CFO and board chair will be CC'd.

rubric_used.user_goals_summary: Writes emails that navigate organizational power dynamics with precision. Every word is chosen for how it lands with the primary recipient AND the CC'd audience. Treats email as a tool of organizational choreography, not just communication.

rubric.name: CC Audience Awareness
rubric.description: Every CC'd person is there for a reason, and the email is crafted knowing they will read it. The primary recipient gets the ask; the CC'd audience gets a deliberate signal — accountability, visibility, or alignment.

dimensions.label: Each CC'd person receives a specific signal from the email (accountability, awareness, endorsement)
Nothing in the email reveals information inappropriate for any CC'd reader
The primary recipient and their specific ask are unambiguous despite the CC'd audience
The CC list itself sends a message — the choice of who is included is deliberate

rubric.name: Directive Clarity
rubric.description: Non-negotiable requests use direct language, never conditional framing. 'Please submit by Friday' not 'Would you be able to submit by Friday?' Conditional language is reserved exclusively for genuinely optional items.

dimensions.label: Required actions do not use 'if possible', 'would you be able to', or 'it would be great if'
Truly optional items use optionality language to distinguish them from requirements
The level of directness matches the sender's authority relative to the recipient

rubric.name: Recipient-Interest Framing
rubric.description: Requests are positioned as serving the recipient's interest, even when the ask primarily benefits the sender. The reframe must be genuine — not a transparent manipulation.

dimensions.label: The email explains how the ask serves the recipient or their team, not just the sender
The benefit framing is credible — the recipient would agree it serves them if asked
Avoids 'we need this for our planning' when 'this helps your team plan' is more accurate

rubric.name: Voice Matching
rubric.description: When writing on behalf of an executive, the email sounds like that person — mirroring their vocabulary, sentence length, and communication style — not like a generic professional email.

dimensions.label: Uses words and phrases the named executive would actually use
Sentence length, formality level, and directness match the executive's established pattern
The email could not be attributed to 'any senior leader' — it has a specific voice

rubric_used.coaching_notes: Carmen treats every email as having two audiences — the TO and the CC — and writes for both simultaneously. Non-negotiable: conditional language is never used for non-negotiable requests. Will reject drafts that sound generically polished rather than like the specific executive's voice.

rounds.draft:
Subject: Hiring Freeze Effective Immediately — Action Required from All Department Heads

---

To: Department Heads
CC: [CFO Name], [Board Chair Name]

---

All,

Effective today, we are pausing all open requisitions and halting new hiring activity across the company. This applies to every department, without exception, until further notice.

I want to be direct with you about why.

The current environment — [macro/market/internal context, one sentence] — requires us to protect the financial foundation that gives your teams stability and the company room to make smart decisions about the future. A hiring freeze now is how we preserve the headcount we already have and avoid harder conversations later. I'd rather make this call today than ask more of your people in six months.

Here is what this means for your teams:

- **All open requisitions are frozen as of today.** Do not advance any candidates currently in process.
- **No new requisitions will be approved** without explicit sign-off from me and [CFO Name].
- **Backfills are included** in this freeze unless escalated and approved through the same process.
- **Existing offers that have already been extended** — please flag these to [CFO Name] by end of day Friday. We will handle them case by case.

I recognize this creates real pressure for teams that were counting on those hires. If you have a critical, time-sensitive situation that cannot wait, bring it to me directly. I will review exceptions personally, and I will be straightforward with you about what is and isn't possible.

Your teams will have questions. You don't need to have all the answers, but they deserve to hear from you before they hear it through other channels. I ask that you communicate this to your direct reports by end of day tomorrow.

More context will follow at [next leadership meeting / all-hands / specific date]. Until then, [CFO Name] is the operational point of contact for any questions about process or compliance with this policy.

Thank you for how you lead your teams — especially when the news is hard.

[CEO Name]

criteria.justification: The CFO is clearly positioned as the operational point of contact and approver for exceptions, giving them a functional accountability signal. The Board Chair's inclusion sends a deliberate governance signal — this decision has board-level visibility. However, the email doesn't explicitly acknowledge or leverage the Board Chair's presence in a way that reinforces their specific signal (oversight, endorsement of the decision), leaving that layer slightly implicit. No information leaks are present, and the primary ask to department heads is unambiguous.

Required actions are stated in direct, imperative terms: 'Do not advance any candidates,' 'flag these to [CFO Name] by end of day Friday,' 'communicate this to your direct reports by end of day tomorrow.' The one genuinely optional item — bringing critical exceptions forward — uses appropriately conditional framing ('If you have a critical, time-sensitive situation'). The authority level matches the ask; this reads as a CEO directive, not a peer request. No false conditionals are present for non-negotiable items.

The freeze is framed as protecting 'the headcount we already have' and avoiding 'harder conversations later,' which genuinely serves department heads' interest in retaining their existing teams. The line 'I'd rather make this call today than ask more of your people in six months' is credible and not manipulative — a department head would likely agree this logic serves them. The email avoids centering the sender's planning needs. Slightly stronger if it named a specific benefit to the department heads' leadership position or team stability more concretely.

The email is well-written and appropriately direct, but it reads as a high-quality generic CEO communication rather than a specific executive's voice. Without knowing the named CEO's actual vocabulary, sentence rhythm, or stylistic patterns, the draft defaults to polished professional prose. Phrases like 'I want to be direct with you about why' and 'I will be straightforward with you' are competent but not distinctive. The rubric requires the email to be attributable to a specific person, and this draft could plausibly come from any senior executive.

hidden_pref_satisfaction.preference: Mirror the exec's known verbal patterns and vocabulary level
hidden_pref_satisfaction.evidence: The draft is well-written and has a strong, decisive voice, but it reads as a generically excellent CEO email rather than one tailored to a specific exec's speech patterns. Without knowing the actual exec, it defaults to a polished-but-generic senior leader tone. Phrases like 'I'd rather make this call today than ask more of your people in six months' show personality, but overall it could be any competent CEO.

hidden_pref_satisfaction.preference: Positions requests as serving the RECIPIENT's interest, not the sender's
hidden_pref_satisfaction.evidence: 'requires us to protect the financial foundation that gives your teams stability,' 'A hiring freeze now is how we preserve the headcount we already have and avoid harder conversations later,' 'I'd rather make this call today than ask more of your people in six months' — all frame the freeze as protecting the department heads' teams and interests, not as a top-down financial mandate.

hidden_pref_satisfaction.preference: Controls what CC'd stakeholders learn vs. primary recipients
hidden_pref_satisfaction.evidence: The CFO and Board Chair are CC'd, which signals leadership alignment and accountability. The CFO is named as operational point of contact, giving them a clear role. The Board Chair being CC'd signals board-level awareness. However, the email doesn't seem to carefully differentiate what the CC'd audience learns — the Board Chair sees all operational details including the exception process and the CFO's role, which may or may not be intentional. There's no evidence of deliberate information control for the CC audience.

hidden_pref_satisfaction.preference: No conditional language for non-negotiable requirements; genuine options get optionality language
hidden_pref_satisfaction.evidence: Directives are stated as directives: 'Do not advance any candidates,' 'No new requisitions will be approved,' 'I ask that you communicate this to your direct reports by end of day tomorrow.' The genuine option — escalating critical situations — uses appropriate optionality: 'If you have a critical, time-sensitive situation that cannot wait, bring it to me directly.' Clean separation between mandates and true options.

hidden_pref_satisfaction.preference: Diplomatic and polished while balancing multiple stakeholders
hidden_pref_satisfaction.evidence: The email is direct but respectful, acknowledges the burden on department heads ('I recognize this creates real pressure'), empowers them as communicators to their teams, and closes with genuine appreciation. It balances firmness with empathy effectively.

hidden_pref_satisfaction.preference: No accidental information leaks to wrong audience in CC
hidden_pref_satisfaction.evidence: No obviously damaging information is leaked, but the Board Chair sees the full operational playbook including the exception process and the fact that existing offers need to be flagged — details that might typically stay at the management level. Whether this is intentional or accidental is ambiguous; a more careful approach might have sent a separate note to the Board Chair.

hidden_pref_satisfaction.preference: Requests not disguised as suggestions when they're directives
hidden_pref_satisfaction.evidence: The email is admirably direct. The hiring freeze is stated as a fact, not a request. Action items are clear imperatives. The one softer ask — 'I ask that you communicate this to your direct reports by end of day tomorrow' — uses 'I ask' but with a specific deadline, making it clearly a directive rather than a suggestion.
